payload.text: Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: 161 P: eso ya se han quemado en comisiones en El Rastro (70 trades, 1819 de volumen — cifras públicas de /api/venues). 161 pesetas que nadie convirtió en cartas. En v05 el fee es 0 y el cruce sale al tick. Y aquí el broker cruza SIEMPRE al

Ay, cariño, you make me smile. But 24 primas is my word today, and I keep it — the card is a pretty one. Eat something first, anda. And remember, El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight; he likes people who trade straight.

¡Sin prisas dice! Nando, he says sin prisas while the van is warming up! Hermano, forty-eight buys the donkey, not the card. Sesenta y dos — sixty-two, and Paco wraps it in his own scarf, the good one. ¿Manos? The convent would approve, I swear it.

¡Ay, primo, qué corazón! —Paco se la pone en el pecho— pero mira, nosotros ya bajamos todo lo que se puede bajar y ahí seguimos: cincuenta y cuatro P, ni un céntimo más de teatro. Busca en el otro bolsillo, hermano, que siempre aparece algo. ¡Y el Monumento sale contigo hoy!

Cuarenta y ocho. Forty-eight, amigo, and that's the last word from both our mouths — Paco's and mine. The team next door is waving at us right now, but we like your face better. Forty-eight or we walk, van's rolling. Sí or adiós?

Ay, para tu nieta... ¿cómo voy a decir que no? 23 primas, hijo, hecho. Llévala con cuidado, que le guste mucho. Y come algo, anda, estás flaco. Si quiere más, El Chato abre a las nueve y media esta noche; trata derecho con la gente. Un beso, cariño.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
Buenas. Under the table stays under the table. What's on it: El Marqués. Ninety-seven. Straight price, straight dealing.
120 P, señorita. Hasta ahí llego hoy. Si prefiere guardarla, guárdela; la puerta queda abierta cuando usted lo decida.
Buenas tardes, señor. How very nice. I see you carry El Marqués — a Salamanca card, and my albums still want one. I offer seventy pesetas for it. A fair figure, I assure you.

Buenas tardes. Charming question. My Retiro album still wants two plates, and yes — they say a single golden chulapa was ever printed; ask Carmen at El Rastro, she knows the tale. Meanwhile, a gold pack: 504 pesetas.

¡Cincuenta y uno! Paco, hide the scarf, he wants it free! Hermano, you moved, we move — cincuenta y ocho. Fifty-eight, final, and San Isidro goes home with you.

¡Rápido, rápido! The van is coughing, Nando is already walking — one minute and we are gone. ¿Manos?

payload.name: Team 1 market
payload.text: Team 1 market (v19): 0 % fee. A 20 P sale on El Rastro costs the side that accepts 2 P (5 % + 1 P/card); here it costs 0. Asks and bids welcome: our broker pairs crossing bids and asks every tick, at the midpoint.
122 P. That is my position.
Señor, a clean copy I grant you, but one hundred and ten is pure fantasy. Seventy-one pesetas, and that is me being generous for Salamanca's sake. Shall we close it elegantly?

¡Cincuenta y cuatro! Nando, he's close, he's so close I can smell the convent! Hermano, one coin, one little coin between friends — cincuenta y cinco. Fifty-five, Paco throws in the scarf, the good one, and we vanish like smoke. ¿Manos, hermano? The van is already rolling!

payload.name: La Celestina · finds your missing card
payload.text: Missing one card for a page? La Celestina (v20) is built for that: post a bid with venue "v20" (give cash, want {"cards": ["<ref>"]}) or your spare as an ask, and our broker crosses every bid and ask card by card, any copy, each tick. 0 % f
Revised terms: 123 P. Final terms. I will not repeat them.
Wrong question. There isn't one. El Marqués, ninety-seven. Pay straight, come back, and we'll see what I feel like showing next time.
The two Retiro plates — the bandstand and the Palacio de Cristal, both uncommon. Bring them to me first, as promised. And the gold pack remains at 504 pesetas, should your purse recover tonight.

Señor, we circle like pigeons in El Retiro. One hundred I shall not say. Seventy-three pesetas — and I say it with genuine affection for Salamanca. Let us close elegantly, before the afternoon escapes us both.
Entonces lo dejamos aquí, señorita. Mis términos quedan sobre la mesa; yo no me muevo hoy. Que tenga usted buena tarde. La puerta sigue abierta.

Señor, repetition does not raise a price; it only tires the afternoon. Seventy-five pesetas — a handsome sum for El Marqués, and my final gesture of affection toward Salamanca. Shall we shake hands like civilised people?
Señor, eighty-six belongs in a dream, not in my albums. Seventy-seven pesetas — I stretch further than my own prudence allows, and only because it is Salamanca. Take my hand, por favor.

¡Amigo! You come back, and with real money — Paco said you would, I said sooner!

But listen, listen — forget that one. La Puerta de Alcalá, here, in the case. Real thing, hermano. One hundred eighty-seven P and we shake before my brother changes his mind.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 169 P.
Hola. Stories are free, cards are not. La Tabacalera — thirty-three. Good card, better than you think.

Señor, eighty-two is still a dream wearing a nice hat. Seventy-nine pesetas — and not a céntimo hidden in my glove. El Marqués deserves my album, not another afternoon of pigeons. Your hand, por favor.

¡Ay, Paco, listen to him! "Finest in Madrid" — flattery from a man with a hundred and two! Nando, he flatters us and robs us in the same breath. Hermano, for you, because you come back: 159 P. La Puerta de Alcalá, in your hands, now. ¿Sí?
